summary: Timer coagulation after node restart causing sustained p99 latency drift for continuous batching
description: Issue summary: After a subset of worker nodes were restarted as part of a rolling OS patch, Nimbus Analytics observed a persistent upward drift in p99 inference latency for requests served by the continuous batching path. Impact: customer reports 10-15% of generation requests hit >2x baseline p99 and occasional 504 timeouts during peak traffic windows. This started immediately after the node restarts and persisted for multiple hours despite traffic leveling. Environment: Dedicated capacity cluster for Nimbus (prod, us-east). Affected lanes are routed to a small set of worker pods that were restarted between 03:10–03:25 UTC on 2026-03-05. Expected: no sustained latency drift after rolling restart. Observed: p95 largely stable; p99 increased from ~220ms to ~650–1,200ms for affected tenants and then slowly drifted upwards over hours.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Deploy rolling restart of worker pool (simulate by restarting 3/10 GPU nodes). 2) Recreate customer-like steady traffic: mixed short (1–3 token gen) and medium (40–80 token) requests at 120 qps. 3) Observe continuous-batcher metrics (batch sizes, linger/ms, flush counts) and per-tenant latency percentiles. 4) Correlate with connection-level timers (keepalive, request arrival jitter) and OS-level clock/ntp drift. Expected result: transient slight disturbances but p99 returns to baseline within a few minutes. Actual: p99 drifted and exhibited periodic waves for ~4 hours.
logs: Relevant snippets: - worker-07 (restarted 2026-03-05T03:12Z): continuous-batcher: timer_reschedule delta=+25ms repeated 120x; flush_count spikes align with flush-coalescence window; - serving-runtime: kv-cache-warmup hits increased (miss rate +18%) across restarted nodes; - net: tcp_retransmits minor; keepalive timeouts observed on ~0.8% of connections; - scheduler: lease_revoke && reschedule churn during restart window. Example: 2026-03-05T03:14:22Z worker-07 batcher timer fired late by 74ms -> flush delayed -> subsequent flush aligns multiple tenants -> p99 spike at 03:14:23Z. Logs stored: s3://redwood-support/nimbus/SUP-658412/logs/ (linked).
investigation_notes: Initial hypotheses: 1) Timer coagulation: upon restart, internal batcher flush timers became aligned (coagulated) across shards leading to periodic large flushes instead of smooth distribution. 2) KV cache cold-start + prefetch contention increased serialization and delayed per-request scheduling. 3) OS-level timer granularity change after kernel patch introduced quantized timer scheduling causing batches to cluster. Actions taken: - Replayed traffic against a restarted node in staging; reproduced p99 waves when system clocks and timer jitter were simulated. - Collected continuous-batcher metrics: linger_ms histogram shifted high, flush_count per interval showed strong peaks. - Kernel config check: restarted nodes had tick parameter unchanged, but C-states/power management differences observed between patched and unpatched images. - Memory pressure not significant; CPU utilization modest. - Correlated with autoscaler: small surge in pending requests triggered wakeups in short bursts. Temporary mitigations applied: scaled up worker pool by +20% to reduce per-node load and reduce alignment impact. Remaining unknowns: precise kernel timer behavior and whether runtime should jitter flush timers on startup to avoid coagulation.
temporary_workaround: 1) Scale out affected dedicated pool by 20% to reduce collision probability. 2) Restarted batcher service on a single affected node to break alignment on 2026-03-05T10:02Z; p99 dropped but waves reappeared after traffic resumed full distribution. 3) Applied per-process randomized jitter on linger window in-flight (feature flag) for the tenant as an emergency mitigation. These actions reduced 504s to near zero and lowered p99 by ~40% for the customer.
resolution_notes: Root cause: timer alignment (coagulation) in continuous-batcher flush scheduling on nodes that had recently restarted combined with increased KV-cache misses. The coagulation was amplified by micro-second level timer skew introduced by the OS patch (worker image x.y.2026-03). Fix plan: - Short term: enable randomized jitter on batcher linger timers during node warmup (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4512). - Medium term: add warmup routine to prepopulate KV cache for incoming tenants post-restart and add health-check gating to hold traffic until warmup completes. - Long term: evaluate kernel timer tuning and consider avoiding rolling restarts that align time-of-day across shards; add scheduled jitter to orchestrator restart order. Rollout notes: staged feature-flag rollout to affected clusters started 2026-03-09 and completed 2026-03-10 with monitored improvement. Follow-ups: file INT- where engineering will add a test to simulate restart-coagulation in CI.
